what_this_is: A founder retiring signatures they previously gave, because two census identities turned out to be one building each. A signature is an attestation and is never deleted or edited: the original ruling stays exactly as it was written, in the ledger that recorded it, and this file records a LATER ruling that supersedes it. Reading both in order tells the whole story; reading either alone would not.
recorded_by: claude-opus-5 (PTF-ST-LOUIS-PUBLICATION-CLEANUP-008B, agent) -- transcription only; both supersessions and the dual-brand confirmation are the founder's, given in the work order, and no row was retired that the founder did not name
why_that_word: SUPERSEDED already exists in contracts.enums.APPROVAL_DECISIONS and is documented as 'replaced by a later decision. Not publishable.' It is writable and is not in PUBLISHING_DECISIONS, which is exactly the semantics required here. No new vocabulary was invented.
how_this_was_found: The bare-chain census names 'doubletree' and 'wingate at wyndham' HID both collisions. PTF-ST-LOUIS-FOUNDER-REMEDIATION-004 and -FINALIZE-007 corrected those names to what each property's own page states, which made each row a name-for-name twin of a sibling identity that had been in the census all along. The duplication was already inside the 114 rows signed at 005; the renames did not create it, they exposed it. PTF-ST-LOUIS-PUBLICATION-READINESS-008A caught it as a slug collision during a read-only publication simulation.

identity_confirmations.founder_ruling: CONFIRMED AS TWO DISTINCT HOTELS. Do not merge or suppress either row.
identity_confirmations.why_the_gate_asks: PTF-MILWAUKEE-PUBLICATION-037 blocked a build over two Hilton brands at one address, because a shared address is exactly how one building gets published twice. The gate is right to stop; a human is what settles it.
why_these_are_distinct: DIFFERENT Marriott property codes: stlff and stlsu. Marriott codes are per-hotel and no two hotels share one -- the same discriminator PTF-COLUMBUS-IDENTITY-CLEANUP-001 relied on to keep three Columbus Embassy Suites apart.
different brands with different source pages
a shared switchboard is ordinary at a dual-brand Marriott property and is not evidence of one hotel
identity_confirmations.note: The two rows carry OPPOSITE pet findings -- Fairfield is pet-friendly and SpringHill is verified-no-pets -- which is only coherent if they are in fact two hotels. Merging them would have published one of the two findings about a building that never made it.
